questions.stem: A reaction in which HEAT is RELEASED is called:
questions.explanation: Exothermic — releases heat (ΔH < 0). Examples: combustion, respiration, many neutralisation reactions. Endothermic — absorbs heat (ΔH > 0). Examples: photosynthesis, evaporation, most dissolution. First law of thermodynamics applies.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: When iron reacts with copper sulphate solution, it DISPLACES copper. This is a:

options.option_text: Single-displacement reaction (more reactive metal displaces less reactive)

questions.explanation: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Iron (more reactive) displaces copper (less reactive) from its salt solution. Blue → pale green colour change. Demonstrates reactivity series. Zinc also displaces copper (Zn > Cu).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: REDOX — shortened 'reduction-oxidation'. Oxidation = loss of electrons (OIL — Oxidation Is Loss). Reduction = gain of electrons (RIG — Reduction Is Gain). They always occur together. OILRIG mnemonic. Example: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (H oxidised, O reduced).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: CaCO₃ (limestone) → CaO + CO₂. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Decomposition — one reactant splits into two or more products on heating. CaCO₃ → CaO (quicklime) + CO₂ at ~825°C is industrially important (basis of cement and lime production). Electrolysis of water — another common decomposition.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: A CATALYST is a substance that:

options.option_text: Speeds up a reaction without being consumed

questions.explanation: Catalyst — alters reaction rate (speeds up via a lower-activation-energy pathway) without being permanently consumed. Enzymes = biological catalysts (enzymatic). Example: Ni in hydrogenation of oils; platinum in catalytic converters of cars; Haber process uses Fe catalyst.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Haber-Bosch process (Fritz Haber, 1909; scaled up by Bosch). N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, using Fe catalyst at ~450°C and ~200 atm. Revolutionised fertiliser production. Nobel Chemistry 1918 (Haber), 1931 (Bosch). Critical for feeding the world's growing population in the 20th century.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Neutralisation: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Exothermic. Forms salt + water. Useful antacid chemistry — Mg(OH)₂ (milk of magnesia) neutralises excess stomach HCl.
